829. Since religion resides in the highest parts of a man, and his lower parts live and shine from these highest parts, and because Muhammad dwells in their minds together with their religion, some Muhammad is always placed in their view. In order that they may turn their faces toward the East, over which is the Lord, he is placed below the Christian center. It is not Muhammad himself who wrote the <term>Alcoran</term> <gloss>Koran</gloss>, but another who performs his duty; nor is it always the same person, but he is changed. At one time it was a man from Saxony who, having been captured by the Algerians, became a Muhammadan. Because he had also been a Christian, he was induced several times to speak with them about the Lord, that He was not the son of Joseph, but the Son of God Himself. Later, others succeeded this Muhammad. In the place where this representative Muhammad has his seat, a fire appears like a torch, so that he may be recognized; but that fire is not visible to others, only to the Muhammadans.

830. Muhammad himself, who wrote the Alcoran, does not come into view today. It was told to me that in the early times he presided over them, but because he wanted to rule over all things of their religion as God, he was cast out from his seat, which he had held among the Papists, and sent down to the right side near the south. Once, a certain society of Muhammadans was incited by malicious persons to acknowledge Muhammad as God. To settle the sedition, Muhammad was lifted up from the lower earth and shown, and then he was also seen by me. He appeared similar to those corporeal spirits who have no interior perception, with a face tending toward black. I heard him speak these words, "I am your Muhammad," and soon he seemed to sink down.

831. Muhammadans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the faith of three Divine Persons, and from that the worship of three Gods and just as many Creators. Furthermore, they are hostile to the Roman Catholics because of their genuflections before images; for this reason they call the latter idolaters and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, that they say "one" but mutter "three," and consequently that they divide omnipotence and make three out of one. They say that they are like fauns <note>mythological woodland spirits, often depicted with horns</note> with three horns, one for each god and all three together for one, and that this is how they pray, how they chant, and how they sound from the pulpits.

832. The Muhammadans, like all nations that acknowledge one God and love what is just and do good from religion, have their own Heaven, but it is outside the Christian one. However, the Muhammadan Heaven is divided into two. In the lower one, they live honestly with several wives, but from there, no others are raised into the higher Heaven except those who renounce their concubines, acknowledge our Lord the Savior, and at the same time acknowledge His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This faith is the means among them by which they are granted ascent by the Lord into the higher Heaven.

833. The fact that the Muhammadan religion has been received by more kingdoms than the Christian religion can be a cause of scandal to those who think about Divine Providence and at the same time believe that no one can be saved unless they are born a Christian. But the Muhammadan religion is not a scandal to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence; these people inquire into where this is, and they also find it. It is in this: that the Muhammadan religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the Wisest of all, and also as the Son of God. But because they have made only the Alcoran the book of their religion, and because Muhammad, who wrote it, has settled in their thoughts and they accord him some worship, they therefore think little of our Lord. So that it may be fully known that this religion was raised up by the Divine Providence of the Lord to abolish the idolatries of many nations, it will be told in some order, but first concerning the origin of idolatries.
